note: Demo flows as data (MK20.1). Narration uses {{placeholders}} resolved against the live dataset at render time, so copy cannot drift from the data the way 'IT Server Hardware ... 48 servers across SYD and MEL data centres' did after the dataset grew to 200 servers across four. An unresolved placeholder renders as a visible gap, never as a stale default.

flows.title: IT server hardware — anomalies, dashboard, clustering

steps.title: Load {{dataset.name}}
steps.narration: Start by loading the server inventory: {{dataset.rowcount}} rows over {{dataset.columncount}} columns. Note the sensitivity badge — this one is {{dataset.sensitivity}}, because it carries contact names and email addresses.

steps.title: Read the schema, not the rows
steps.narration: The schema panel on the left is what would be sent to a model: column names, an inferred type, a distinct-value count and a null rate. No cell values. Check the PII flags before going further.

steps.title: Ask about expired warranties
steps.narration: This prompt goes out with the schema and no rows. The answer comes back as a query to run here, against data that never left the device.

steps.title: Generate a dashboard
steps.narration: Each card states where its number came from. A card that could not be resolved against the loaded rows says so rather than showing a figure — that distinction is the point of the page.

steps.title: Cluster in the Insight Lab
steps.narration: k-means runs entirely on this device with no model call at all. Cluster on CPU and RAM utilisation and the overloaded servers separate out.

steps.title: Switch to {{dataset.name}}
steps.narration: Time-series readings for the same fleet. Loading a second dataset replaces what the schema panel offers, so the next question is asked against these columns.

steps.title: Ask about memory leaks
steps.narration: A question no single column answers. The model proposes how to look for it; the looking happens here.

steps.title: Check what was disclosed
steps.narration: Session totals: prompts sent, entities detected and replaced, tokens counted. Read it as a record of what left the device, which is the only number on that page anyone should act on.

flows.title: Same pipeline, opposite outcomes — public aggregate then patient records

steps.title: Load a real public dataset
steps.narration: {{dataset.name}} — {{dataset.rowcount}} rows, published under CC BY and attributed on the card. Sensitivity {{dataset.sensitivity}}. Nothing in it identifies a person.

steps.title: Nothing to redact, and the pipeline says so
steps.narration: Read the schema panel. No column is flagged as personal information, because none is. Watch what the privacy stage reports on the next step: the honest answer for this dataset is zero entities, and a filter that invented some would be worse than useless.

steps.title: Ask a question of public data
steps.narration: The schema goes out, the rows do not — the same rule as always, even though there is nothing here worth protecting. That is the point: the control does not switch on and off depending on how sensitive the data looks.

steps.title: Now load something with people in it
steps.narration: {{dataset.name}} — a SYNTHETIC fixture, badged as such on its card: it imitates the shape of MBS claims and every name, date of birth and Medicare number in it is fabricated. {{dataset.rowcount}} rows, sensitivity {{dataset.sensitivity}}. Nothing real is at risk in this demo, and the pipeline does not know that.

steps.title: Same panel, five PII columns
steps.narration: The schema panel now flags patient_name, dob, medicare_number, provider_name and patient_id. Compare it against the last dataset: the pipeline is identical and the reading is completely different, which is what the control being real looks like.

steps.prompt: Top 10 specialties by total benefit paid
steps.title: Ask a comparable question of patient records
steps.narration: A structurally similar question. Open the privacy review before sending and read the placeholder mapping: what leaves the device, what stands in for it, and what comes back. Note the limitation the page states — placeholders are not consistent across requests (PL1.1).

steps.title: Read the two sessions side by side
steps.narration: One dataset produced no detections and one produced many, from the same code on the same path. That contrast is the demonstration, and it is the only claim this flow makes: enforcement is ordered, recorded and inspectable when traffic is in path. It is not a claim that nothing can bypass it — six bypass classes are tracked as a test corpus.
